observations.text: Sure, that's fine. What would you like to know?
The process starts as we — the sales employees — receive the customer's quotation request. The intended outcome is that we send the quotation to the customer.
After we receive the customer's quotation request, I check the customer information in the CRM.
After checking the customer information, I create the quotation document using the quoting system, pulling in the pricing information.

After creating the quotation, it depends on the amount. If it's over 1,000,000 yen, the manager has to approve it first, and then we send it to the customer. If it's at or below 1,000,000 yen, we send it directly. Also, if it's the end of the month, we send a summary of the quotation information to Accounting.

Yes, we send a summary of the quotation information to Accounting at month-end, in addition to sending the quotation to the customer. It happens after we create the quotation, but I don't know if it's exactly at the same time or after the quotation is sent — that's not something I have details on.

When the quotation is over 1,000,000 yen, the manager approves the quotation. I don't know which system the manager uses for that. The reason for the approval is credit risk management. As for what happens if the manager doesn't approve, I don't know.
We send the quotation to the customer by email.
I'm not sure if they are the same thing. I create the quotation document in the quoting system, and then I send the quotation to the customer by email, but I don't know if it's the same document.
I send the summary of the quotation information to Accounting using Excel. I don't know the specific details of what's in it beyond that it's a summary of the quotation information.
I don't know why we check the customer information.
